subject: Data Exposure Coordination: SLA Windows, Forensic Access, and Subprocessor Liaison
messages:
From: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@hexabank.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: PeakCloud Security <security@peakcloud.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential data exposure — immediate coordination request

Alex —

We’ve identified anomalous access patterns that may have exposed a small set of customer records in the Redwood-hosted job for our payments workload. We need to coordinate next steps for evidence preservation and regulator timelines. High-level asks from our side: 

- Confirmation of internal detection/acknowledgement SLA and who will be the Redwood liaison.
- What evidence you can export (logs, request/response payloads, KV cache dumps) and standard formats.
- Your typical handover window for complete forensic evidence and whether you offer temporary forensic access (read-only) to our security team.
- Whether any subprocessors (storage, analytics) need to be engaged and expected timelines for their responses.

This is time-sensitive — regulators want an initial customer notice assessment within 48 hours if material. Please let me know next steps and preferred secure channel to transfer keys/artifacts.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Reddy
Head of Security, HexaBank
maya.reddy@hexabank.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@hexabank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — immediate coordination request

Maya —

Thanks for the flag. I’m Alex (on-call for HexaBank) — we’ll be the primary liaison. Quick plan outline and timelines from Redwood: 

- Ack and triage: acknowledgement within 4 hours of receipt (you’ve got it), initial triage and scope call within 12–24 hours.
- Substantive customer-impact determination: target within 48 hours; we’ll escalate to legal immediately if we see confirmed customer data exposure.
- Evidence preservation: we take a forensic snapshot (logs + request metadata) immediately and freeze relevant instances and KV caches.
- Evidence handover: we can provide redacted exports and a secure forensic bundle within 7–14 days depending on size and export complexity. If HexaBank needs read-only forensic access to a snapshot, we can enable a temporary SFTP+VPN channel for up to 7 days after legal authorization.
- Subprocessors: we’ll surface impacted subprocessors within 24 hours; typical turnaround from cloud/storage subprocessors is 48–72 hours for evidence pulls.

Actions from Redwood now: Ben is starting the collection checklist; Laura will confirm contractual notification windows and any DPA constraints. Please confirm the scope: which customer IDs, date windows, and types of data you believe were affected. Also confirm whether HexaBank prefers evidence to ship via SFTP or via a secure shared drive link.

I’m looping Ben, Laura, and Tessa for their items below.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Lead, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@hexabank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — immediate coordination request

Maya / Alex —

Technical checklist (short):

1) Preserve: snapshot the affected serving instances, capture full request logs (timestamp + request_id + user_id), export KV cache ranges for impacted sessions.
2) Collect SIEM/event logs (we can provide JSON export).
3) Hash and sign exported bundles and provide checksum.
4) Mask PII for shared artifacts unless HexaBank requires full payloads for analysis (we can provide redacted + certified full export under legal authorization).

Attachment: forensic-checklist.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — contains step-by-step commands and expected file names we’ll produce.

Preferred transfer: encrypted SFTP endpoint. We’ll generate a time-limited user and rotate keys post-transfer. If HexaBank prefers, we can instead provision temporary, read-only access into a locked snapshot environment (requires formal access request and NDA accessory).

I’ll kick off the snapshot now and post a short status update in this thread when the first bundle is ready.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: PeakCloud Security <security@peakcloud.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@hexabank.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — immediate coordination request

Hi all —

PeakCloud here (storage subprocessor for the affected Redwood job). We’ve received a request from Redwood’s support team and can prioritize a data export. A couple of notes: 

- Our standard turnaround for low-latency exports is ~48 hours once we have job IDs and the time ranges.
- Cross-border exports: if the data contains EU-origin personal data and HexaBank’s regulator requires data residency controls, we need a signed data transfer addendum or documented legal basis for transfer outside the EU.
- We can produce access logs and object-level access history; snapshots will be delivered as encrypted tar.gz files.

Please send the PeakCloud job id(s) and an ingress endpoint. We’ll coordinate directly with Ben on the secure transfer.

—PeakCloud Security Ops
security@peakcloud.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@hexabank.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — immediate coordination request

Maya —

Following up on contracts and regulator timelines. Per the Redwood DPA (Section 6.3): Redwood will notify customers and affected controllers "without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware" of a personal data incident. In practice, we are committing to the operational timeline Alex outlined (ack within 4 hours, impact decision by 48 hours) where reasonably possible.

A few legal points: 

- We can provide redacted forensic artifacts immediately; full payloads that contain customer PII will require HexaBank to execute the access request form (attached) and, if applicable, an ancillary redaction agreement for regulator-facing materials.
- Subprocessor engagement: Redwood will coordinate and request exports from subprocessors. We will share expected ETA per subprocessor (usually 48–72 hours).
- Cross-border transfer: if PeakCloud needs additional contractual paperwork to permit transfers, please route that to legal@peakcloud.com; we will assist in signatures or DPA addenda where required.

Attachment: sla-summary.xlsx (spreadsheet) — summary of our internal SLAs and handover windows for evidence.

We’ll also record this as HubSpot deal HS-9482 and create a DocuSign envelope for any required addenda (DocuSign-Envelope-0a1b2c3d).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
